host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

neighborhood_overview:
Calle Feria is one of the streets with the greatest personality in the city of Seville (Andalusia), and is located in the Old Town District. It begins in Calle Madre María Purísima de la Cruz (Old Viriato) and ends in Calle Resolana after a long and straight path.

description: Apartment of one bedroom with double bed and a double sofa bed in the neighborhood Santa Cruz, next to the Giralda and in one of the streets with more tourist charm.
neighborhood_overview:
Santa Cruz is one of the most important and popular neighborhoods of Seville (Spain), corresponding with a part of the old medieval Jewish quarter of Seville, next to the district of San Bartolomé.
Located in the center of the city, it borders to the west with the surroundings of the Cathedral; To the south with the gardens of the Alcázar; To the east with the Gardens of Murillo and to the north with the street Santa Maria the White.
It has its origin in the old Judería of Seville, when the king Fernando III of Castile conquers the city, concentrated in Seville the second most important Jewish community of Spain, after the one of Toledo.

After the expulsion of the Jews in 1483, the neighborhood of Santa Cruz plummeted, until at the beginning of the XIX century the recovery of the neighborhood was decided, for which the street of Mateos Gago opened (the only street relatively wide of the neighborhood ) And redeveloped the square that bears his name.

name: 2BR Private Terrace, Parking, Tapas & Market
description: Perfect for families or two couples looking for a local experience. This comfortable flat is located in a quiet, typical Andalusian patio. However, go straight out the door and you are in for a treat. Seville's oldest market is only a few steps from our apartment, a large outdoor square with tapas bars is a block away and the Cathedral is a leisurely 20-minute walk. The 2BR apartment has an equipped kitchen & baby accessories. Enjoy a private terrace with views of the nearby 13th century church.
neighborhood_overview: Our apartment is quiet but the neighborhood is lively.  It can make a 90 year old feel like a 20 year old. We are in the old town or “Casco Antiguo” of Sevilla, making it easy to walk to all of the major sights of Seville. Straight out the door you will find the vibrant Feria Food Market, the Mudejar Museum and a great little bakery. Just a few more steps will take you to the famous Macarena Church or the fun Plaza of the Alameda de Hercules. The neighborhood, known as the Alameda area, has a true small town feel that allows you to see everyday Sevilla life. The Alameda is where Sevilla (young, old, hippy, conservative, gypsy and foreign) comes together. Its lively plaza as well as its surroundings has many different restaurants, making it a perfect place to "tapear".
host_about:
Pepe and I are a creative couple who met in Spain through our common interest in art. I am originally from New Jersey, exit 4 for those who need to know. I landed in Seville over 22 years ago and decided to stay mostly for the cheap wine and great fish. Pepe is from Seville but he will tell you his mother is from Huelva, making him half "choquero" (the term used for people from coastal Huelva). His passions are photography, nature and salty air. Some of his photos decorate our home as do a few of my collages. I worked 12 years for the Andalusian government in environmental projects but after falling in love with olive oil, left my job and became an expert olive oil taster.  In our free time we enjoy trying to figure out how to restore our 45 year old sailboat, hiking and taking long motor bike rides through Spain. We fall under the category of live to eat and not eat to live and like to try the newest tapas bars in Seville. We will be more than happy to share our foodie-findings as well as interesting places in Andalusia that we have enjoyed exploring by foot, by boat, by motor and by accident.

Calle Feria is one of the streets with the greatest personality in the city of Seville (Andalusia), and is located in the Old Town District. It begins in Calle Madre María Purísima de la Cruz (Old Viriato) and ends in Calle Resolana after a long and straight path.

It owes its name to the Thursday fair or market that has been held there since the 13th century, being the oldest in the city. Nowadays the sidewalks are filled with small stands or stalls where antiques and second-hand objects are mainly sold, although in its origins all kinds of items were offered.

Walking through this neighborhood, we will have the opportunity to know much of the history of the city, with buildings such as the Hospital de la Santa Caridad or the Chapel of the Brotherhood of the Carretería and the Baratillo, with the "bullfighter" atmosphere that can be seen in it. There was a day when, as its name suggests, this neighborhood was a large open space between the Triana gate and the Torre del Oro. host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

neighborhood_overview:
The Arenal is one of the most traditional and emblematic neighborhoods of Seville, during the 16th and 17th centuries it was one of the most important port areas in the world, a meeting point for Sevillians.
It is a bullfighting district par excellence, in which is the bullring of the Real Maestranza of Seville. The Arenal has a lot of religious devotion, the main brotherhoods in Holy Week roam its streets. It's definitely a neighborhood full of art and life.
host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

name: Apartament in the Historic quarter
description: Charming apartment, perfectly equipped and luminous. It is a first floor at the city centre of Seville. It takes one minute to go to the "Alameda" and twelve minutes to go to the Giralda Chatedral on foot.
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is situated in the heart of Seville and boasts a unique character. Every Thursday morning, an antique and second-hand market takes place on the "Feria" street, which has been a tradition since the 13th century. This market is held in a specific section of the street where the apartment is located. Additionally, this area is significant during the Easter festivities, as some of the most important Easter brotherhoods in Seville, such as "Macarena," pass through this street.

The apartment's location is very convenient, as it only takes a minute to walk to the "Alameda de Hercules," five minutes to reach the "Plaza de la Encarnación ( las Setas)," and a 12 min walk to the Cathedral.

The "Feria" street is home to several historic buildings, including the "Monte-Sion" chapel, the church of "San Juan de la Palma," the thirteen-century church known as "Omnium Sanctorum," and an 18th-century food market.

The Arenal is definitely one of the most traditional and iconic neighborhoods in Seville. During the 16th and 17th, it was one of the most important port areas in the world, as a result of the discovery of America and trade with the Indies. Today it is still a place of great activity and meeting point of the Sevillians, especially around the world of bullfighting, the theater, the opera and the brotherhoods.

Walking through this neighborhood, we will have the opportunity to know much of the history of the city, with buildings such as the Hospital de la Santa Caridad or the Chapel of the Brotherhood of the Carretería and the Baratillo, with the "bullfighter" atmosphere that can be seen in it. There was a day when, as its name suggests, this neighborhood was a large open space between the Triana gate and the Torre del Oro. host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

During the 16th and 17th, it was one of the most important port areas in the world, as a result of the discovery of America and trade with the Indies. Walking through this neighborhood, we will have the opportunity to know much of the history of the city, with buildings such as the Hospital de la Santa Caridad or the Chapel of the Brotherhood of the Carretería and the Baratillo, with the "bullfighter" atmosphere that can be seen in it. host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

Wellcome to my house!!. I am a member of AIRBNB from January 2015 and my apartment was published the 13th of February. I was born in Madrid and I have been living in Seville for ten years. I studied Forestry Engineering in Madrid and I have worked for the Enviromental Department of Andalusia region and associated companies since then.
In 2007, I lived three months with a great Irish family in county Tipperary and later on, I left for Dublin. I was taking English lessons in Emerald school and I was working for a travel agency during one and a half year. When I was younger I was living in Paris for four months to improve my French but  to be honest it is a little bit rusty at the moment. 
I am quiet person but full of curiosities. I like studying and l became Pharmacist last year in Seville University. I love Andalusian people, beaches and villages, especially Cadiz, it is fantastic and not very far from Sevilla, just one hour driving.
I like going to Madrid to visit my small family, specially I enjoy being with my 94 th years old grandmother and my little nieces, whom I miss a lot.
So, now that you know something about me , let me tell you that Sevilla is a must-see; it is full of happinness and calmness and its weather, cuisine and cultural heritage deserve a special mention.
As I told you in my first paragraph, I am a new hostess, so it is going to be the first time I offer my home to other people and I am very excited with this project. To finish my presentation I would like to share with you a coutation special for me knowdays. “Beginning things is having nearly finished”.
I would really love you to stay in my house, get away from it all, enjoy the city, recharge batteries, pamper yourself……. and if you fancy and Seville inspire you….. might be the moment to think about starting whatsover dream has been knocking your mind …..
Enjoy Seville,
Ana

Bienvenidos a mi casa!!. Soy miembro de AIRBNB  desde enero de 2015. Soy una madrileña que lleva viviendo en Sevilla desde hace más de diez años. He vivido en Dublín durante un año y medio donde estuve trabajando en una agencia de viajes y aprendiendo inglés. En general soy una persona tranquila y familiar. Me encanta conversar, pasear por el campo y disfruto mucho con la buena comida. Me encanta la playa y las andaluzas son espectaculares, especialmente las de Cádiz.
Creo que ciudades como Sevilla hay que verlas, están llenas de alegría a la vez que de sosiego y culturalmente y gastronómicamente son difíciles de igualar.

Un abrazo, Ana

The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. This fantastic apartment is located in the famous Alameda de Hercules, one the most charming and particular urban areas of the old town, where culture, art and leisure mix.

Nowadays, the Alameda de Hercules is the oldest public garden, not only in Spain, but in Europe, and the largest square in the center of Seville. It’s named after the Hercules’ statues which were placed on two columns that were brought from an old roman temple. Another two columns from the Plaza de España were not added until the XVIII Century.

Very well located apartment in the Triana neighborhood, on Alfarería street, next to Río Guadalquivir, La Cartuja Technological Park and Torre Sevilla shopping center. Very close to the city center. Easy access by car and direct access to the highway. Bicycle (Sevici) and bus rental public service a minute away. Triana Market, bars and restaurants within 5 minutes.
Long stay rental, minimum 60 days.

neighborhood_overview:
Triana is a historic neighborhood, with pottery and flamenco tradition. Their markets of supplies, Betis Street and Paseo de la O, which face the Guadalquivir River are world-renowned. Crossing the bridge of Triana, in front of the street Betis we find the Plaza de Toros of the city, the Real Maestranza of Seville.
This is a very popular neighborhood, with a lot of life in its streets, and in which there are plenty of well-known bars and restaurants.
Very close also, although in the opposite direction, is the Isla de la Cartuja, in which the 1992 Universal Exposition was held and in whose Monastery there is since then the Centro Andaluz de Arte Contemporáneo (CAAC), to which you can walk.

 The contrast and harmony between contemporary interventions and preserved elements provide magical journeys through time. Experience the city's legacy from within with all modern amenities.

neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located in a unique enclave, within the monumental and commercial area of historic downtown Seville. Literally next to the Church of El Salvador and a few minutes from the Santa Cruz neighborhood, it allows you to forget about the car.
With the Cathedral on one side and the Plaza Encarnación Market (Metropol Parasol) on the other, it is an area characterized by masterfully connecting the old and the contemporary, offering one of the most charismatic corners of the city.

Nos encanta el arte en todas sus formas, leer, viajar, cocinar, los buenos platos acompañados de un buen vino, y compartidos con personas amigas.
Durante nuestros viajes siempre hemos buscado sitios acogedores, tranquilos, cómodos y limpios, en pleno corazón de las ciudades donde nos encanta perdernos andando, para respirar la autenticidad de cada lugar y descubrir lo inesperado.
Así que cuando, conjuntamente a otros proyectos profesionales que desarrollamos en el ámbito socio-cultural, hemos empezado a dedicarnos a remodelar y gestionar apartamentos, hemos querido ofrecer las mismas cosas que vamos buscando.
Estaremos encantadas de daros la bienvenida y de proporcionar informaciones sobre la oferta cultural, artística y social y toda las aclaraciones necesarias a que vuestra estancia sea inmejorable.
¡Hasta pronto!

LOS HUMEROS
The neighborhood of the Humeros was located outside the walls of the gate of Goles, which was named from the entrance of the monarch Philip II in 1570 as the Royal Gate. The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. This busy area is the place to come for clothes, sporting goods, jewellery and Sevilla Feria fashion: shawls, flamenco dresses, castanets and fans... It originated in the old Jewish quarter of Seville, when King Ferdinand III of Castile conquered the city, concentrated in Sevilla's second largest Jewish community in Spain after Toledo.
After the expulsion of the Jews in 1483, the Santa Cruz plummeted, until the early nineteenth century the recovery ward was decided, for what the street Mateos Gago (the only relatively wide street of the neighborhood opened ) and the square that bears his name was redeveloped.
In the current Plaza de Santa Cruz it was once located the parish of Santa Cruz, originally gave its name to this district.

During the 16th and 17th, it was one of the most important port areas in the world, as a result of the discovery of America and trade with the Indies. Today it is still a place of great activity and meeting point of the Sevillians, especially around the world of bullfighting, the theater, the opera and the brotherhoods.

There was a day when, as its name suggests, this neighborhood was a large open space between the Triana gate and the Torre del Oro. neighborhood_overview:
The neighborhood of San Vicente is located in the northwest of the historic center of Seville, it is bordered by the Guadalquivir River to the west and the Alameda de Hercules to the east. It is a neighborhood known for its many squares, churches and convents. Next to St. Lawrence Square is the Basilica of the Great Power, home to one of the city's most revered images of Christ: Jesus of the Great Power.
The monastery of San Clemente is the oldest in Seville. It was founded in 1248 by Ferdinand III and here rest several members of the royalty, such as Maria de Portugal - the mother of Pedro El Cruel, who built the Alcázar. In the neighborhood of San Vicente were built the convents of Santa Clara and Santa Rosalia.
Places of interest: Churches and convents; Plaza de San Lorenzo; Torre de Don Fadrique - defensive tower in the Convent of Santa Clara; Dark Camera in the Torre de los Perdigones; Traditional bars and restaurants.

The apartment is located on Calle Rodrigo de Triana.

Triana is one of Seville´s authentic neighbourhoods. It´s located on the west bank of the Guadalquivir, a short walk across the river from the centre.

Historically the neighbourhood of craftsmen, sailors and dockworkers, today Triana still plays an important role in Seville's cultural heritage. It is one of the spiritual homes of flamenco culture, and home to the world renowned Triana pottery. Here you will find workshops and ateliers selling both traditional and modern ceramics.

Betis Street, which runs alongside the river, provides stunning views of the old city centre by day and night, and is a popular destination after hours with its wide range of restaurants, bars and clubs. At the far end of the street, by the Triana Bridge, is the 150 year old food market built over and beside the ruins of St. George's Castle - the Castillo San Jorge, once home of the infamous Inquisition.

El Centro is the neighbourhood at the very heart of historic Seville. With the majestic Cathedral at your doorstep, el Centro begins at the Plaza de San Francisco, location of the elaborate City Hall, one of the best examples of plateresque architecture in Spain.

The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. This busy area is the place to come for clothes, sporting goods, jewellery and Sevilla Feria fashion: shawls, flamenco dresses, castanets and fans... The Palace of the Contesa de Lebrija is nearby, home to the famous Pan Mosaic which dates from roman times.

The Arenal is definitely one of the most traditional and iconic neighborhoods in Seville. During the 16th and 17th, it was one of the most important port areas in the world, as a result of the discovery of America and trade with the Indies. Today it is still a place of great activity and meeting point of the Sevillians, especially around the world of bullfighting, the theater, the opera and the brotherhoods.

Walking through this neighborhood, we will have the opportunity to know much of the history of the city, with buildings such as the Hospital de la Santa Caridad or the Chapel of the Brotherhood of the Carretería and the Baratillo, with the "bullfighter" atmosphere that can be seen in it. There was a day when, as its name suggests, this neighborhood was a large open space between the Triana gate and the Torre del Oro. host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

Pepe and I are a creative couple who met in Spain through our common interest in art. I am originally from New Jersey, exit 4 for those who need to know. I landed in Seville over 22 years ago and decided to stay mostly for the cheap wine and great fish. Pepe is from Seville but he will tell you his mother is from Huelva, making him half "choquero" (the term used for people from coastal Huelva). His passions are photography, nature and salty air. Some of his photos decorate our home as do a few of my collages. I worked 12 years for the Andalusian government in environmental projects but after falling in love with olive oil, left my job and became an expert olive oil taster.  In our free time we enjoy trying to figure out how to restore our 45 year old sailboat, hiking and taking long motor bike rides through Spain. We fall under the category of live to eat and not eat to live and like to try the newest tapas bars in Seville. We will be more than happy to share our foodie-findings as well as interesting places in Andalusia that we have enjoyed exploring by foot, by boat, by motor and by accident.

The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. This busy area is the place to come for clothes, sporting goods, jewellery and Sevilla Feria fashion: shawls, flamenco dresses, castanets and fans... The Palace of the Contesa de Lebrija is nearby, home to the famous Pan Mosaic which dates from roman times.

Heading northwest towards the Guadalquivir River is the Museo de Bellas Artes, the city’s Fine Art Museum, one of the most important art museums in Spain after Madrid’s Prado. The collection includes important work by Murillo and early Velazquez.

Triana is a vibrant old quarter in Seville, situated on the left side of the Guadalquivir River and connected to the city by the iconic bridge of Isabel II, otherwise known as Puente de Triana.
Formerly known as Seville’s gypsy neighborhood, Triana has evolved into a lively idiosyncratic area packed with charming paved streets, ceramic shops, pretty churches, atmospheric tapas bars, and beautiful traditions.

Although Roman and Muslim influences can be observed all over Triana, this charming neighborhood has managed to shape and retain its own distinct character. Illustrious bullfighters and passionate Flamenco singers and dancers may not roam the streets like they used to, but the marks they have left behind are still alive in the area, and that’s particularly what makes Triana one of the most colorful areas in Seville.

name: NEW! CENTRAL PENTHOUSE WITH PRIVATE TERRACE + A/C
description: This penthouse boasts a large, private terrace with stunning views. It's located in the historical centre of Seville, next to Europe’s oldest public square, La Alameda de Hercules, where an eclectic array of dining and entertainment is offered. It is a bright and airy space which has been newly renovated and refurbished. It has a double bedroom, open-plan living room and fully equipped kitchen. There is WiFi, A/C and ELEVATOR.
neighborhood_overview:
The "Alameda de Hercules" is Europe's oldest public square and gardens, dating back to 1574. It is a recreational space offering a wide range of historical places of interest to visit. There are countless gastronomic possibilities to whet your appetite, no matter whether you are a local or a tourist, and numerous terraces to enjoy the sun and live music playing out into the late hours of the evening.

We also have one of the most beautiful and liveliest markets in Seville, which is none other than the "Feria" street market, where you can try the local delicacy of "pescaito frito" (fried fish), various cold meats, wines, and even sushi ... what better way than to pass away your time here in Seville!

• Alameda de Hercules 50m away.

neighborhood_overview:

There are three UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the district, the Cathedral of Seville, the Alcazar and the Archivo General de Indias:

- The Gothic Cathedral was built in 1403 on the site of a former mosque of which the Almohad minaret, the Giralda, was retained as a bell tower. It is the largest Gothic building in Europe, and houses the tomb of Christopher Colombus.
- The Alcázar, built by the Moors in 712, was converted into a Christian royal residence in 1248.
- The Archive of the Indies was designed as a trade exchange of American treasures by Juan de Herrera under the orders of King Phillip II of Spain. It was never used in that role and in 1784 King Charles III of Spain decided to store all documents relating to the conquest of the Americas.

The renovated living room is the perfect place to enjoy a glass of wine and take in the view of Seville’s charming, cobblestone streets below. With high-quality mattresses (1 double bed and a sofa bed that sleeps 2), the apartment can accommodate up to 4 guests comfortably.
neighborhood_overview:
The house is located in the historic center. You can walk to all the places of cultural interest of our beautiful Seville. The Plaza de Toros, the Teatro de la Maestranza, las mushrooms, the Museum of Fine Arts, the Golden Tower, the Cathedral with its famous Giralda or the Museum of Contemporary Art are just some of the nearby points.

The neighborhood is very quiet and perfectly located to walk to any place of interest. The commercial heart of Seville consists of the trinomial Sierpes, Tetuán and Campana, so do not hesitate to visit it.

The Guadalquivir River is very close, so you can go for a walk along its shore or cross any of its bridges to go to neighborhoods as famous as Triana.
host_about:
Hi I'm Ignacio!

I travel a lot - for work and - the best part - also for pleasure. I love meeting new people, tasting new food, experiencing new cultures. I have lived in different countries and continents so traveling is very much part of my DNA as well as my life experience. I have used Airbnb in the past and I am now happy to host fellow travelers.

I live in Marid but I spend most of my time traveling so I have decided to share my beautiful apartment with you.

But don't worry, you will be well taken care of when I am not in town thanks to my friends at Minty Host, who are there to help my guests with anything they need. On my side, I will be more than happy to share with you the city I love - its main landmarks but also its fantastic restaurants, bright squares, and bustling bars.

Enjoy your stay!

***
Hola soy Ignacio!

Soy una persona curiosa y es lo que me ha llevado a vivir en distintos países, conocer culturas y viajar mucho.

Vivo en en Madrid pero estoy prácticamente todo el tiempo fuera por viajes, así que he decidido compartir este increíble apartamento con todos. Pero no os preocupéis, estaréis muy bien atendidos ya que mis amigos de Minty Host me ayudan a cuidar a mis huéspedes cuando no estoy en la ciudad.

Me encanta viajar y todo tipo de viajes, de ocio y descanso, de turismo, de aventura, a grandes ciudades, pequeños pueblos o lugares salvajes, con familia, amigos o incluso solo. Disfruto mucho conociendo gente y aprendiendo de sus culturas.

He utilizado Airbnb para viajar en numerosas ocasiones y ahora me he decidido a ser anfitrión. Me gusta ofrecer un buen servicio, que la gente quede encantada de la experiencia y que disfruten en la vivienda, del barrio y de la ciudad en la que he vivido gran parte de mi vida y de la que estaré encantado de compartir sus mejores secretos.

Os invito a disfrutar de la estancia!

Champú en la ducha, sábanas planchadas en la cama con almohadas confortables, cocinas limpias y agradables y una recomendación para almorzar a la vuelta de la esquina.

Pero a medida que más y más propietarios de viviendas urbanas exploran el mercado de alquiler de corta estancia, incluso a los anfitriones más espabilados les resulta cada vez más difícil proporcionar un alto nivel de hospitalidad para sus huéspedes.

Por esta razón nace KEYWii. Porque no todo el mundo tiene tiempo de leer y contestar cada una de las solicitudes de reserva; ni de lavar y planchar sábanas y toallas, limpiar la casa, sacar la basura, adecuar la casa, dejar y recoger las llaves… y repetir el proceso para los siguientes huéspedes.

Sabemos que “el mejor alquiler es aquel que se siente como un hogar y se gestiona como un hotel”.

Como la mayoría de negocios ingeniosos, KEYWii nace del deseo de satisfacer una necesidad y de un don personal para destacar en logística, hospitalidad y elegancia.

neighborhood_overview:
El Centro is the neighbourhood at the very heart of historic Seville. With the majestic Cathedral at your doorstep, el Centro begins at the Plaza de San Francisco, location of the elaborate City Hall, one of the best examples of plateresque architecture in Spain.

The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. This busy area is the place to come for clothes, sporting goods, jewellery and Sevilla Feria fashion: shawls, flamenco dresses, castanets and fans... The Palace of the Contesa de Lebrija is nearby, home to the famous Pan Mosaic which dates from roman times.

Heading northwest towards the Guadalquivir River is the Museo de Bellas Artes, the city’s Fine Art Museum, one of the most important art museums in Spain after Madrid’s Prado. The collection includes important work by Murillo and early Velazquez.

The main industry of the neighborhood has traditionally been pottery with the manufacture of tiles, earthenware, bricks, etc., so you can find handmade pottery workshops.
At the end of the Puente de Triana, the Plaza del Altozano is reached, where the current Triana market opens, in whose lower part you can find the remains of the old Castillo de San Jorge. This fortress was the seat of the Inquisition since 1481, although its initial construction dates back to 1171.

neighborhood_overview: Santa Cruz is the most popular quarter in Seville and it has its origins in the old Jewish quarter of Seville. This quarter was inhabited by the Jews ever since Seville was recaptured by Ferdinand III, King of Castile, until these were ejected in the 15th century. Located in the center of Seville, Santa Cruz quarter reaches down to the Cathedral, the gardens of the Alcázar (palace) and Jardines de Murillo (Murillo gardens). It is, therefore, a landmark and a touristic zone and it is accessible through Mateos Gago street, the most touristic and commercial street of the quarter. While having a walk in this zone, you can get to know more about its history, by contemplating the Moorish and Jewish features that so characterize this place. Furthermore, you can go into the narrow streets, which run in an irregular criss-cross pattern and lead to the patios sevillanos (traditional Sevillian patios) or squares, such as Plaza de la Alianza or Plaza de doña Elvira. It is probably the most special neighborhood in Seville, famous for its history, its idiosyncrasy and its meaning. Discover it little by little, Triana deserves it.

The origins of Triana date back to the Tartessian era.

This population center on the right bank of the Betis River (Roman name for the Guadalquivir), served the Roman legions to establish a camp, close to Itálica and in front of Híspalis. It was the Almohads who built the first bridge that linked it with the city, a boat bridge located where the famous Triana Bridge is today.

In the 15th and 16th centuries, Triana was present in those maritime expeditions that aspired to discover new worlds. His School of Seafarers instructed many navigators of the time who took part in voyages such as the arrival of Christopher Columbus to America or the Tour of the World by Magellan and Elcano, whose departure was also made from these shores. The apartment is located in the historic, monumental and commercial center of the city. The Cathedral, just 400 meters away, is the focal point of Sevillian life. It is an area of bustling pedestrian streets, characterized by its large number of shops, many of them with more than a century of existence. At a distance of a delicious walk of no more than 10 minutes away, we enter the pedestrian area of the Cathedral's environment, with its Giralda, and the Barrio de Santa Cruz, Juderia and Triana.

The surroundings of our houses are full of charming traditional houses, palaces, mansions, flowery courtyards and, above all, history.

name: Bright and modern 2D apartment - Seville center
description: The modern, light-filled 2 bedroom vacation apartment in the heart of the city center in Seville is the perfect choice for exploring the stunning sights nearby. Just steps away you’ll find many of the city’s most famous architectural wonders, including the San Leandro Convent (5 min), the Seville Cathedral (15 min) and the beautiful Jardin de Morilla Park (15 min). For trips further away, there are several large bus stations nearby (10 min).
neighborhood_overview:
The most central area of Seville - between Plaza de la Encarnación and Plaza Nueva - is famous for its rich Moorish architecture, but in addition, shopping and gastronomy fans will also find their place in this neighborhood.
Here you can find a large number of international brands, as well as artisans creating leather goods, traditional fans and hand-embroidered clothing.
In addition to many restaurants and bars to choose from, visitors will marvel at the museums, architecture and history of this charming area part of the city.
This area hosts the areas of greatest tourist interest, including the Sevilla Setae -the largest wooden structure in the world-, New Square, museums recognized by UNESCO (The Cathedral, the archive of the Indies and the Alcazar), La Giralda and numerous cathedrals, each with its unique charm.
If you want to discover the oldest part of the city on foot, this is the ideal place for your stay.

neighborhood_overview:
San Vicente is a residential neighbourhood notable for its many squares and churches, located in the northwest of the historic centre. Minutes from the major sights and attractions, it makes an ideal base to explore an authentic part of the city and enjoy some of Seville's most renowned local tapas bars.

Historic churches worth visiting are San Vicente - a fine example of gothic-mudejár architecture built during the 15th century – and the Basilica del Gran Poder, home to one of the most revered and famous images of Christ in the city. The procession of the "Cristo del Gran Poder" is a quintessential part of Holy Week in Seville.

San Vicente is bordered on the west by the Guadalquivir River and the riverside is popular for walking, cycling and running. neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located on Rodrigo de Triana street.

Triana is one of Seville´s authentic neighbourhoods. It´s located on the west bank of the Guadalquivir, a short walk across the river from the centre.

Historically the neighbourhood of craftsmen, sailors and dockworkers, today Triana still plays an important role in Seville's cultural heritage. It is one of the spiritual homes of flamenco culture, and home to the world renowned Triana pottery. Here you will find workshops and ateliers selling both traditional and modern ceramics.

Betis Street, which runs alongside the river, provides stunning views of the old city centre by day and night, and is a popular destination after hours with its wide range of restaurants, bars and clubs. At the far end of the street, by the Triana Bridge, is the 150 year old food market built over and beside the ruins of St. George's Castle - the Castillo San Jorge, once home of the infamous Inquisition.

The neighborhood is bounded by Menéndez and Pelayo avenues, Puerta de la Carne, Santa María la Blanca, San José, Vírgenes, Águilas, San Esteban, and Puerta de Carmona streets. They delimit and enclose a nucleus endowed with certain factors of its own.
History
The neighborhood originated during the Andalusian era. When Fernando III of Castile conquered the city (1248), the neighborhood of San Bartolomé, together with the neighborhood of Santa Cruz, became the Jewish Quarter of Seville, by order of the King who converted three mosques that existed in this area into synagogues (and that would later be converted into Christian churches: the church of Santa María la Blanca, the church of San Bartolomé and the church of Santa Cruz, demolished in 1814 to create the Plaza de Santa Cruz).

The most central part of Seville, between Plaza de la Encarnación and Plaza Nueva, is famous for its wealth of ancient Moorish architectural monuments, but shopping addicts and food lovers will also find many things to do here. Here you will find a wealth of international brands as well as local artisans making leather goods, traditional fans and hand-embroidered clothing. Apart from the many restaurants and bars to choose from, visitors will be amazed by the museums, architecture and history in this charming area of the city.
This area is home to most of the city's best-known tourist attractions, including Metropol Parasol, the world's largest wooden structure, Plaza Nueva, a trinity of UNESCO-recognized museums (the Cathedral, Architecture of the Indies and Alcázar), La Giralda and an overwhelming number of ancient cathedrals, each with its own unique appeal. Today it is still a place of great activity and a meeting point for Sevillians, especially in the world of bullfighting, theater, opera, and brotherhoods.

The airport bus leaves you at Torre del Oro or Plaza de Armas and then it's a 10-minute walk to the apartment.

Taxi from the airport €22.50/fixed rate.
You don't need a car to visit the city on foot. If you come by car you can leave it in the Arenal Parking lot. When you stay 3 days or more the price is €11/day. You also have the Paseo de Colón parking lot.
And of course there are always bicycles, there are stops everywhere, and it's a wonderful way to get to know the city.

The City Hall leads you to the main shopping area with it´s famous parallel shop-lined streets: Sierpes and Tetuan. Its impressive Jewish quarter, with narrow and labyrinthine streets is just a few minutes from the apartment. The Cathedral, Archivo de Indias and Alcázar, a World Heritage Site, are also just a few minutes away on foot. neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located on Calle Juan Sebastián Elcano, next to triana.

Triana is one of Seville´s authentic neighbourhoods. It´s located on the west bank of the Guadalquivir, a short walk across the river from the centre.

Historically the neighbourhood of craftsmen, sailors and dockworkers, today Triana still plays an important role in Seville's cultural heritage. It is one of the spiritual homes of flamenco culture, and home to the world renowned Triana pottery. Here you will find workshops and ateliers selling both traditional and modern ceramics.

host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

description: Spacious and comfortable apartment, recently renovated, in the historic center of Seville. It has 3 bedrooms: 1 with a double bed and 2 with 2 single beds each, a spacious living room with a sofa. Fully equipped kitchen and two full bathrooms. neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located just across the Triana bridge, and in the historic center of Seville.Triana is the most vibrant neighborhood in the city, marked by its deep and unique history, first as a marine neighborhood, then as a potter's neighborhood and finally as the cradle of flamenco artists, bullfighters and dancers.
Staying in the old town next to Triana is living the essence of Seville, it is feeling part of a special and unique atmosphere.

name: A11.  9. Gaseno. Cozy Little Peaceful Dúplex
description: In the center of Seville, next to the Real Maestranza de Caballería and monumental area of the city. In one of the most representative historical buildings of the Arenal district is Apartamentos ALMANSA 11 Coliving. In an area of cultural interest where you will find exhibitions, concerts, restaurants full of life and fun that will certainly encourage and help make your stay happy.
neighborhood_overview:
The Arenal is one of the most traditional and emblematic neighborhoods of Seville, during the 16th and 17th centuries it was one of the most important port areas in the world, a meeting point for Sevillians.
It is a bullfighting district par excellence, in which is the bullring of the Real Maestranza of Seville. The Arenal has a lot of religious devotion, the main brotherhoods in Holy Week roam its streets. It is a neighborhood full of art and life.
host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

neighborhood_overview:
The Alameda de Hercules area has become one of Seville's most cosmopolitan spaces. It is a meeting point for Sevillians and visitors from all over the world, where you can enjoy a varied gastronomic offer, have a coffee, see cultural activities (concerts, exhibitions...), or just walk along the entire square. During the day it is a place where families and groups of friends predominate walking and taking tapas, and at night it becomes the epicenter of the heterogeneous Sevillian movida.
Also, in just 7 minutes you can reach such emblematic sites as La Macarena or San Lorenzo.
If you come as a family, you can get to Isla Magica in less than 10 minutes, and if you are a sports lover or concerts you can get to the Olympic Stadium in 25 minutes.

The vibrant Alameda de Hércules is a recently renovated tree-lined square, popular with families during the day and with those who enjoy night-life after dark. The Alameda has many cafés, modern terrace bars and clubs which stay open late into the night.

Heading north you'll find the Macarena gate, within a long stretch of the original city defensive walls, and the Basilica of the Macarena, home of one of Seville's most venerated religious images of the Virgin Mary.

neighborhood_overview:
The cozy and charming Santa Cruz neighborhood of Seville was the Jewish neighborhood of Seville in medieval times, up to the Spanish Inquisition. This hidden gem is perfect for those who want to seep into the rich history, art and culture of Seville.

The Moorish architecture is vibrant and the streets smelling of jasmine are narrow and form a maze, which makes it easy to get lost and stumble across the area's many convents, palaces, and churches. It is a main tourist district and there are many small shops and some craft shops as well as art galleries. It borders with the Jardines de Murillo, Real Alcázar, Calle Mateos Gago and Calle Santa María La Blanca / San José. This neighborhood is the place where many of Seville's oldest churches are located and the home of Seville Cathedral, including the converted minaret of the ancient Arab Giralda mosque.

Seville airport is easily accessible by taxi (20 minutes) or by bus (1 hour).

neighborhood_overview:
El Arenal is a quiet neighborhood known for its history and cobblestone streets. This neighborhood was once a large open space with a sandy floor, located between the Triana gate of the old wall and the Golden Tower, and was the main location for much of the city's port activity. It is now surrounded by trees, charming and quiet, with restaurants, pubs, and historical monuments.

It is located on the east bank of the Guadalquivir River, west of the old Jewish Quarter, Santa Cruz, and south of the Museo and Alfalfa neighborhoods. Its name comes from the sandy nature that this eastern bank of the river used to have. Some of the neighborhood's historic sites are the Torre del Oro, the 13th-century Moorish watchtower, the Reales Atarazanas, the royal shipyards, La Real Maestranza, Seville's bullring and the second most important in Spain, after the Plaza de "Las Ventas" in Madrid, Teatro de la Maestranza, Plaza de Toros de la Real Maestranza and Mercado del Arenal.

name: A11. 7. Duque Octavio. El hogar.
description:

Exterior, with two large windows facing Galera Street. Tall ceilings, over 4 meters that give a sense of space. It stands out for its brightness.

host_about:
Tras trabajar en sectores tan diversos como las finanzas o la vela y despues de  22 fuera de Sevilla, mi ciudad natal, volví para adquirí este emblemático edificio del Arenal. Corría el año 2010, la crisis económica era una realidad palpable, el inmueble, ocupado por inquilinos de renta antigua, estaba casi en estado de ruina, y la Gerencia de Urbanismo dejaba sentir su aliento para que se actuara.  La situación no era nada facil.

Aunque soy economista, siempre me ha entusiasmado la arquitectura y disfruto en obras y reformas. Me encanta descubrir el potencial que ciertos espacios tienen aunque su aspecto sea negativo debido a un mal mantenimiento o una reforma desacertada. A nivel personal he tenido la fortuna de compartir tiempo con buenos diseñadores y arquitectos de los que siempre he procurado aprender.

Para mi, este proyecto suponía una fuerte inversión y la necesidad de contraer una gran deuda en momentos difíciles. Pero este precioso edificio había pertenecido a mi familia, y la ilusión por restaurarlo y sacarlo adelante me hizo decidirme a ello con gran pasión y convencimiento de lo que hacía. Además, veía un gran potencial en él y la posibilidad de crear una estructura económica sostenible que fuera haciendo frente a los intereses y amortización de la deuda contraida.

Tras llegar a un acuerdo con los inquilinos de renta antigua para su desalojo durante 2010 es en enero de 2011 cuando comenzamos las obras que duran hasta marzo de 2012. 

Se ha dotado al edificio de una moderna infraestructura en saneamientos, suministros y telecomunicaciones, sin perder el sabor original con el que fue creado.

Para ello se ha respetado una máxima; Sanear, limpiar, mantener y reutilizar. Como ejemplo de ello podemos admirar la robusta solería hidráulica, o  los coloridos mosaicos y azulejos que vieron nacer el edificio. En la misma linea observamos como se ha restaurado el total de la carpintería original de balcones, puertas y ventanas, que no son tan prácticos como las modernas a la hora de insonorizar o aislar, pero dan otro aroma. En la monumental fachada, hemos procurado respetar y sacar a la luz cada uno de los muchos detalles que ya tenía.

Con el edificio terminado y los apartamentos funcionando, sabemos que queda mucho por mejorar y estamos lejos de la perfección. El inquilino que viene no disfruta de lujos ni sofisticaciones pero sí encuentra un ambiente acogedor, espacios bonitos, luminosos, gente amable y cosas hechas con cariño. Procuramos además que nuestros precios sean ajustados y accesibles para la mayoría con el fin de que los apartamentos se vivan y se disfruten.

Tengo la ilusión que Almansa11, además de ayudar al crecimiento y desarrollo de esta ciudad, sea también testigo de muchos momentos de felicidad y alegría :-)

A place where good things happen...

description: Beautiful apartment located in the heart❤ of Seville, a few minutes walk from the Bullring, Plaza Nueva, Cathedral, Giralda and Triana Bridge. Enjoy a few days in the traditional and charming Arenal neighborhood, with a magnificent atmosphere any time of year. Feel at home in this ☀bright☀ and cozy apartment, located on the second floor of a typical Sevillian house that combines traditional details, such as its tiled floors, with delicate and careful decoration.
neighborhood_overview:
Our apartment is located in the El Arenal neighborhood. This neighborhood has its origin in a large open space, covered with sand, between the city's ancient walls and the banks of the Guadalquivir River.
This open space was used in the past to serve as the city's port, with good proof of this being the existence in this place of the Reales Atarazanas, which constituted the naval industry owned by the Crown of Castile in the city, remaining operational between the 13th and 15th centuries.
Today, El Arenal is a neighborhood with a fantastic location, in the heart of Seville's historic downtown, between the Santa Cruz neighborhood and the river, within walking distance of most of the city's points of interest, with a great nightlife, a wide range of gastronomy, shopping and culture thanks to the Teatro de la Maestranza and the Museum of Fine Arts, the second most important art gallery in Spain, also just minutes from our accommodation.

neighborhood_overview:
Triana is located on the east bank of the Guadalquivir River and is separated from the old intramural area of the city by the river dock that runs along its historic channel.

The Triana bridge that crosses the dock connects it to downtown.

According to mythology, the goddess Astarte, fleeing from the amorous pursuit of Hercules, mythological founder of the city of Seville, came to take refuge on the western bank of the Guadalquivir, founding Triana.

The origin of its name has also aroused interest among researchers. Traditionally, it was linked to its past as a Roman colony founded by Trajan, the emperor born in Italica, Trajana-Triana. According to some authors, the name comes from a compromise formula between the Celtiberians and the Romans, tri, "three", from the Roman and ana, "river", of Celtiberian origin, since in that area the river was divided into three. This is what Justino Matute Gavira maintains in his work Apparatus to describe the history

Mi nombre es Javier y me gustaría ofrecerles una estancia en Sevilla única e irrepetible.

Atentamente.

Seville is a city of neighborhoods, small cities within the city itself, where each of them has its own personality, its peculiarities, its preferred clientele, and even its customs. However, no area of downtown Seville has experienced such a radical and spectacular change in the last couple of decades as the Alameda de Hércules.

The Alameda de Hércules has a very interesting history, starting with an important fact, and it is the oldest public garden not only in Spain, but in Europe, and it is the largest square in the center of Seville. It was created in 1574, and owes its name to the statues of Hercules that were placed on two columns brought from an ancient Roman temple. The two columns on the other side of the square were not added until the 18th century.

It is one of the most cosmopolitan spaces in Seville, where you can meet visitors from all over the world, whether they are foreigners who have come to study, live, or simply spend a few days.

name: Estudio con Terraza en Suites Machado
description: A bright and flirty apartment. Its Sevillian terrace and its original hydraulic floors give it a cozy and very cheerful character. It mixes current and modernist styles, has beautiful half-point arc windows. Its decor combines the classic furnishings of its spectacular comfort with the contemporary touch of its chaise longue. The kitchen is coveted and modern, and the bathroom has a double sink with stylized period shapes.
neighborhood_overview: The Santa Cruz neighbourhood where Suites Machado is located is the historic and monumental epicentre of the city of Seville. This section of the city is known for its palace manors, museums and churches with a wealth of Andalusian Baroque religious art. There are hidden corners that once made up Seville’s former Jewish Quarter and that surrounded the Royal Palace, which is one of the oldest operating palaces in Europe. The Real Alcazar in Sevilla is, together with the almighty Cathedral, only a few meters away from Suites Machado. Moreover, the neighbourhood is home to elegant tapa bars and nooks dedicated to Flamenco, as is the case of Sala Fabiola—an exclusive location that maintains the essences of the most traditional Flamenco—is waiting to be discovered by tourists. The street itself, where Suites Machado is located, offers several cultural gems, including the only section still standing today of the city’s former Jewish Quarter.
host_about: Manager Pablo Barriga Le Bel has a degree in Hotel Management from Seville’s prestigious Hoteling School.  After one first successful year of Suites Machado (more than 1000 guests), he decided to begin with Airbnb as host. Prior to creating this personal project, this native Sevillian of French-Spanish descent, worked at a number of elegant hotels and travelled with world.  In the family home where he grew up, he combined elegance with comfort and beauty. He is a wonderful host, versed in several languages, to guarantee a warm professional and personal welcome. His guests enjoy the pleasing experience of living in an authentic 17th Century Sevillian palace home, but with 21st Century comfort.

host_about:
Hola,

Soy Olga, creadora y directora de CH Apartments.

Nos encontramos en un edificio histórico del año 1850, ubicado en el corazón de Sevilla, que hasta hace un año había sido mi casa. En este lugar crecí y viví algunos de los momentos más importantes de mi vida.
En 2019 di un paso adelante en mi carrera profesional, y decidí transformar mi casa en un espacio donde la gente pudiera empaparse de la vida y la cultura de nuestra ciudad. 

Aquí, descubrirás que cada rincón ha sido pensado y preparado para el máximo disfrute y confort de nuestros huéspedes. Cada uno de los 6 apartamentos guarda rincones diferentes e increíbles. Hemos querido respetar y preservar los elementos más significativos que desde siempre han habitado el edificio, para fusionarlos con todas las comodidades e innovaciones de nuestros días. 

Todos ellos cuentan con altos techos de madera pintados a mano e iluminados con tecnología LED, dormitorio con cama extra-grande y cabeceros de terciopelo con conectores USB. Dos Smart TV, en dormitorio y salón; baños con ducha o bañera y papel pintado. 
Algunas de las paredes están forradas con porcelánico de Porcelanosa, otros disponen de balcón con vistas directas a la calle Daoíz, patio típico andaluz o terraza exterior privada en la última planta. 

Cada detalle cuenta. Por ello, preparamos cada reserva para que te sientas como en casa, para que vivas una auténtica experiencia y disfrutes de la ciudad como lo hacemos nosotros mismos.

¡Te estamos esperando!

description: Quiet and stylish apartment located in the heart of the Triana neighborhood, seconds from the main artery in the area, Calle San Jacinto and 5 minutes from the center of Seville. neighborhood_overview:
Triana is the most vibrant neighborhood in the city, marked by its deep and unique history, first as a maritime neighborhood, then as a potter's neighborhood and finally as the birthplace of artists, bullfighters and flamenco dancers.
Staying in Triana is living the essence of Seville, it is feeling part of a special and unique atmosphere.
Triana is separated from the city center by the majestic Guadalquivir River, you will only have to cross its bridges, enjoying the best views of Seville, to find yourself in the historic center.
The area has all the amenities and services: supermarkets, bars, restaurants, shops, pharmacies, etc.

description:
Stylish and cozy apartment located in a quiet building of typical Sevillian construction in the heart of the historic center of Seville.
The apartment has 2 bedrooms, 1 with a double bed and the other with 2 single beds (although it can be configured with 1, if you need more space). Full bathroom, fully equipped kitchen and large outdoor dining room with sofa bed.

Its impressive Jewish quarter, with its narrow and labyrinthine streets, is just a few minutes from the apartment. The Cathedral, Archivo de Indias and Alcázar, a World Heritage Site, are also just a few minutes away on foot. The area has numerous bars and restaurants where you can enjoy the excellent Sevillian gastronomy and its famous tapas. The commercial area is 2 minutes away, where you will find multiple stores, shops and supermarkets.
In addition, the vibrant and charming neighborhood of Triana is just a 15-minute walk away, which you will reach after crossing the beautiful bridge over the Guadalquivir River and from where you will enjoy the best views of the city.

Its locations is great to see the city and it's walking distance to all of the best places to visit in Seville.

host_about:
Hola,

Soy Olga, creadora y directora de CH Apartments.

Nos encontramos en un edificio histórico del año 1850, ubicado en el corazón de Sevilla, que hasta hace un año había sido mi casa. En este lugar crecí y viví algunos de los momentos más importantes de mi vida.
En 2019 di un paso adelante en mi carrera profesional, y decidí transformar mi casa en un espacio donde la gente pudiera empaparse de la vida y la cultura de nuestra ciudad. 

Aquí, descubrirás que cada rincón ha sido pensado y preparado para el máximo disfrute y confort de nuestros huéspedes. Cada uno de los 6 apartamentos guarda rincones diferentes e increíbles. Hemos querido respetar y preservar los elementos más significativos que desde siempre han habitado el edificio, para fusionarlos con todas las comodidades e innovaciones de nuestros días. 

Todos ellos cuentan con altos techos de madera pintados a mano e iluminados con tecnología LED, dormitorio con cama extra-grande y cabeceros de terciopelo con conectores USB. Dos Smart TV, en dormitorio y salón; baños con ducha o bañera y papel pintado. 
Algunas de las paredes están forradas con porcelánico de Porcelanosa, otros disponen de balcón con vistas directas a la calle Daoíz, patio típico andaluz o terraza exterior privada en la última planta. 

Cada detalle cuenta. Por ello, preparamos cada reserva para que te sientas como en casa, para que vivas una auténtica experiencia y disfrutes de la ciudad como lo hacemos nosotros mismos.

¡Te estamos esperando!

neighborhood_overview:
Triana is one of Seville´s authentic neighbourhoods. It´s located on the west bank of the Guadalquivir, a short walk across the river from the centre.

Historically the neighbourhood of craftsmen, sailors and dockworkers, today Triana still plays an important role in Seville's cultural heritage. It is one of the spiritual homes of flamenco culture, and home to the world renowned Triana pottery. Here you will find workshops and ateliers selling both traditional and modern ceramics.

Betis Street, which runs alongside the river, provides stunning views of the old city centre by day and night, and is a popular destination after hours with its wide range of restaurants, bars and clubs.
